title: Verbal clash; substance often agrees on this head
source_text: XLVII. Ex his vero facile colligitur, Protestantes & Pontificios, in hac quae-stione quidem, sibi invicem verbis contradicere, sed tamen de re ipsa inter eos esse consensum. Etenim, si tollantur voces ambiguae & contentiosae, & res eadem terminis aliis exprimatur, Pontificii non affirmant, ut patet, quod Protestantes negare inten-dunt, dum inficiantur quemquam per justitiam inhaerentem coram Deo justificari. Neque vicissim Protestantes impugnant quod defendunt Pontificii, dum verbis plane contrarium affirmant, nempe justitiam illam inhaerentem esse causam formalem nostrae coram Deo justificationis. Ita ut tota difficultas pendeat ex vario usu vocis justificandi, quam illi quidem uno sensu, hi vero alio usurpant.
pass_a_gloss: But from these things it is easily gathered that Protestants and Papists in this question indeed contradict one another in words, yet that there is agreement between them about the thing itself. For if ambiguous and contentious words are removed and the same thing is expressed in other terms, the Papists do not affirm, as is plain, what the Protestants intend to deny when they deny that anyone is justified before God by inherent righteousness. Nor in turn do the Protestants impugn what the Papists defend when they affirm in plainly contrary words that that inherent righteousness is the formal cause of our justification before God. So that the whole difficulty hangs upon the varying use of the word justify, which the one side uses in one sense, the other in another.
pass_b_english: On this question words clash, but the thing often agrees once ambiguous terms are removed.
Difficulty hangs on different uses of justificare.
